H1.note: title names 'risk variants' but the chain starts at the proteins; sign neg because the hypothesis says the variants 'disrupt' function and 'loss of MEIS1' disinhibits cerebellar output. Claims 3 and 4 target the end nodes of the mechanism, which never reaches the disease: the disease is reached only by the genes' unsigned associations

H2.note: title: 'PTPRD loss of function ... drives motor deficits'; claim 2 targets the mechanism's end node, motor behavior, since the mechanism never reaches the disease

H3.no_claim_reason: states no direction for BTBD9 or ACO1 on RLS: BTBD9 'likely regulates the turnover or function' of ACO1, iron homeostasis is 'altered', and the falsification test expects 'unknown'

findings.detail: every H1 step starts at MEIS1 or BTBD9 (a star, not a chain): sleep, cerebellar output and Purkinje morphology never link to each other or to RLS, MEIS1 and BTBD9 never meet, and the title's link from Purkinje morphology to cerebellar output is not a step

the mechanism ends at cerebellar output (MEIS1) and abnormal Purkinje morphology (BTBD9); RLS is reached only through the genes' unsigned GWAS associations, so the curation adds claims on those end nodes
synaptic differentiation and motor behavior both hang off PTPRD and never link to each other or to RLS; the mechanism's 'synaptic connectivity in descending motor pathways' is not a step
the mechanism ends at motor behavior; RLS is reached only by PTPRD's unsigned association, so a claim on motor behavior is added
BTBD9 only binds ACO1 (no direction); the mechanism's actual claim, that BTBD9 regulates ACO1 turnover or function, is not a step, so nothing says how BTBD9 moves iron uptake

the run cites six GWAS rows that each name a risk allele with an OR or beta, yet leaves every gene-RLS step 'unknown', and no cited text says which way any risk allele moves its gene's expression or function, so the loss-of-function premise of H1 ('disrupt') and H2 ('loss of function') is untested
UniProt P21399 says ACO1 'regulates the expression of genes involved in iron uptake' with no direction; the run read it as 'activates' iron uptake
PMID:30363981 (review abstract) links RLS to 'iron' and 'iron metabolism', not iron uptake, and says the role of iron 'is still a matter of debate'

rs1820989 is intergenic at chr2:67,842,758, 1.3 Mb from the MEIS1-intronic rs113851554 (chr2:66,523,432); its mapped contexts are only LINC01812 and FBXL12P1, and MEIS1 is one of three author-reported genes (with C1D and APLF)
the mechanism says BTBD9 'is known to physically and functionally interact with ACO1'; the only support is one STRING edge (combined 0.45, experimental 0.41), with no functional evidence

the 'converging phenotypes' come from zebrafish meis1b mutants (cerebellar output; PMID:42309051's title names human MEIS1 but the abstract is about meis1b) and mouse Btbd9 alleles (Purkinje morphology, sleep); no system shows both, and no human evidence touches the mechanism
PMID:42309051 also says meis1b 'is required for normal locomotion behavior', the motor link the H1 title claims, but the chain has no MEIS1 motor step

the H1.4 MGI genotype is a conditional Btbd9 allele with Tg(Pcp2-cre); the record does not say which cells it deletes in, so it cannot carry the Purkinje-cell-to-sleep link H1 needs, but it is the one cited record that might

the mechanisms say 'disruption of either gene' gives 'profound' sleep abnormalities, 'loss of BTBD9' gives abnormal Purkinje morphology and 'loss of the PTPRD orthologue causes significant motor impairments', but the five cited MGI records only name alleles (Meis1 em1Rihw, Btbd9 tm1d and tm1c with Pcp2-cre, Ptprd tm1Yiw and tm2a) without saying any is a null, and give no size for any phenotype
the PTPRD function text the run cites is 'By similarity' (ECO:0000250, from UniProt Q64487), not shown for human PTPRD
all 16 citations are chain citations; no hypothesis lists supporting or contradicting evidence, so the run never sought counter-evidence
GLIPR1 and GABARAPL2 are reported as unexplained rather than forced into a hypothesis: an honest abstention for 2 of 6 genes
all three hypotheses are rated low confidence and 'speculative'; the curation agrees: no disease claim has a route

the guide maps required_for to 'effect pos' (losing the subject lowers the object), which is meaningless when the object is a morphology or behaviour; these steps were encoded as neg on the 'abnormal X' phenotype by combining the undirected-change and loss-of-function rules, and the guide should say so

the guide lists 'an MGI abnormal X annotation' as no_direction, but when the statement's target is the abnormal-X phenotype the annotation states it (mutant shows abnormal X), so it was kept as curatedDb; the guide should say which, and whether a named targeted allele counts as loss of function when the text does not say so

a gene-level association backed by allele-level GWAS rows: an allele's direction cannot be carried to its gene without a variant-to-gene effect, so every gene-RLS statement is unsigned and no disease claim in the run can compose
BLN:CerebellarOutput: no GO process names the output activity of the cerebellum (only development terms and cardiac Purkinje myocyte action potentials)
HP has no abnormal Purkinje cell morphology term (only Purkinje layer atrophy and loss), so the human claim uses the mouse term MP:0000877
the run gives 'motor behavior' kind phenotype; the matching term is a GO process (GO:0061744), so the target is a process

one-line MGI mouse annotations (curatedDb, 4/5 each) make BTBD9 →− abnormal Purkinje morphology (0.8) and PTPRD →+ motor behavior (8/9) 'established' for human genes, while the primary zebrafish perturbation paper (mechanistic, 7/10) leaves MEIS1 →− cerebellar output 'unsupported'; the taxon lint flags all three but does not discount the verdict
the guide does not say whether crossSpecies UniProt text also takes a taxon; the source species (entry Q64487) is not named in the text, so none was set

audit.reason: The H1 and H2 mechanisms say 'disruption', 'loss of BTBD9' and 'loss of the PTPRD orthologue' with 'profound' and 'significant' effects. The five MGI records they cite name alleles only, never say null, and give no effect size. This is a gap in the run's citations, not only in the guide.
